items.title: Doc Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 28, 1995
items.q: I joined Sam Wooding and went to Europe with that band... I recorded with Sam Wooding in Paris.

ctx.x: No, no, no. And my next recording I did in Spain, in Barcelona, with Sam Wooding’s band. Sam Wooding. You never heard of him?

items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: So they were replaced. And so now, we got fellows like Jerry Blake, Doc Cheatham.

ctx.x: So they were replaced. And so now, we got fellows like Jerry Blake, Doc Cheatham. And a queer thing happened to me which I had no business to agree to at that time. And I'm warning all young pianists, don't agree to that anymore. He said, Arthur Lyons said to me, 'Now, the big band leaders now are not playing.' 'They take the baton and stand up.' You know. So, I agreed with him because I didn't want to work no more than I had to work. See, I never did care much for work.
